title: feat: split sign-in loss into GitHub's side and ours
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
38% of sign-in starts never complete. Nothing said whether those people dropped at GitHub or hit a failure in our own callback — and the two have opposite fixes (a second provider vs. a bug).

- Records `sign_in_returned` when GitHub sends the user back with a code.
- `started → returned` is loss on GitHub's side; `returned → completed` is loss on ours.
- Only a callback carrying a `code` counts: a denial returns without one, which is GitHub-side.
- The Better Auth route pattern is `/callback/:id`, not the resolved path, so the provider comes from `params.id` — a `/callback/github` match never fires. The test caught this before it shipped.
- `auth_flow_funnel` gains `sign_in_returned`, `pct_returned` and `pct_completed_of_returned`. Validated against staging: 1 endpoint modified, no deletions.

Measured first: a double-click explanation was ruled out — sub-2s gaps between starts occur *less* than Poisson predicts (5 observed vs ~7.5 expected over 287 gaps), so the 38% is real.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: Following the sign-in trail
gist.blurb: The auth garden has a new trail marker: GitHub returns are now counted separately from completed sign-ins. Much easier to see where a wandering bee actually lost the path.
gist.summary: Auth-flow analytics now records `sign_in_returned` when GitHub redirects back with an authorization code, adding `pct_returned` and `pct_completed_of_returned` to the `auth_flow_funnel` so GitHub-side drop-off is separated from callback completion.
gist.impact: Maintainers can now distinguish sign-ins that never return from GitHub from those that return but do not complete in Pollinations’ callback, making the next auth improvement much more targeted.
